chunks: 4653 - And Ali, peace be upon him, said:
"It is recommended for a man to approach his wife on the first night of the month of Ramadan because of the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
'It has been made lawful for you, on the night of the fasting, to be intimate with your wives.'

key_terms.أَهْلَهُ: his wife; his spouse in this context
key_terms.الرَّفَثُ: sexual intimacy; here specifically sexual intercourse
key_terms.الصِّيَامِ: fasting; the ritual fast observed in Ramadan
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the time of obligatory fasting
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: recommended; a meritorious act in law

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by al-rafath in the verse about the nights of Ramadan fasting?
ai.summary: This report states that intimacy with one's wife on the first night of Ramadan is recommended, based on the Quranic allowance for marital relations during the nights of fasting. It also explains the term al-rafath in the verse as meaning sexual intercourse, clarifying the legal sense of the passage.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4653 - Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
"It is recommended for a man to approach his wife on the first night of the month of Ramadan because of the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic:
'It has been made lawful for you to be intimate with your wives during the nights of fasting' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:187),
